definition: Self-determination theory is a psychological framework that explains behavior in terms of motivation, especially the role of autonomy in shaping how people think and act. In this packet, it is used to suggest that having more usable work autonomy can help people generate more ideas.

reasons: The packet uses self-determination theory only as the framework for a specific teleworking/idea-generation study; it does not support the broad general description of the theory as a general explanation of behavior centered on autonomy and motivation.
The field label should not broaden the sense beyond what is in the packet, and the packet supports a study context in organizational psychology rather than a general cognition definition.

The definition’s claim that self-determination theory is “a psychological framework that explains behavior in terms of motivation” and that it specifically emphasizes “autonomy in shaping how people think and act” is not directly supported by the supplied packet text (the packet only uses the theory as a lens for a specific study).

The definition’s claim that the packet uses self-determination theory to suggest “having more usable work autonomy can help people generate more ideas” is supported in substance by the packet’s proposal that teleworking facilitates idea generation by enhancing work autonomy, but the first sentence contains unsupported general theoretical claims.
